newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba surprises mkt with profit hike.
newsitem.headline: Veba surprises mkt with profit hike.

text.p: German diversified utility giant Veba AG took the market by surprise on Wednesday when it reported a 25 percent hike in nine-month net profits.
The increase, to 1.227 billion marks ($821 million), exceeded all expectations.
The company tantalised the markets further when it forecast that earnings would keep growing in full-year 1996 and that it expected to maintain earnings growth levels seen up to now.

"We are confident that we will see a clear increase in earnings in the full year, based on the earnings growth seen in the first nine months of the year," the group said in a statement from its Duesseldorf HQ early on Wednesday.
The group said fewer special charges and operating and structural measures to improve competitiveness in all areas of the group's activities would also help to boost profitability.
The group's restructuring plans also helped it compensate for only marginal growth in sales in the period of 1.4 percent to 55.31 billion marks, from 54.55 billion marks a year previously.
Pre-tax profits increased to 2.51 billion marks from 2.19 billion marks in the first three quarters of the year.
The profit increase was warmly welcomed on the Frankfurt bourse and Veba shares rose to an all-time high of 86.90 marks in early trading.

"The group net profit figure is above our expectations. There were two external elements in these figures -- the bad weather and the oil price -- but everything else comes from Veba's own internal restructuring," said Lynn Reinhardt, utilities analyst at BZW in Frankfurt.
"These figures also come against a background of trading disadvantages in Veba's trade, transport and services sector and weakness in the chemicals unit," said Reinhardt.
"Veba's story is the strength of its management and its ongoing programme of restructuring," she added.
Peter Antes, utilities analyst at the Munich-based Bayerische Vereinsbank, said he was raising his earnings per share (EPS) outlook for Veba for 1996 to 5.10 marks from 4.80 marks after the results.
"These figures were surprisingly positive. They seem to have taken Veba themselves by surprise, as they are better than what was indicated at the half-year stage," said Antes.
Electricity sales in the third quarter were higher than the group had been expecting, Veba said, due to the cold summer and increased electricity exports.

However, turnover in the first nine months fell because of a drop in prices and the effects of the disposal of its hazardous waste management unit, WESTAB, which has been incorporated into a joint venture with Ruhrkohle Umwelt GmbH.
There was also strong growth in the Veba's oil trade, where a decline in turnover in the petrochemical business was compensated for by higher prices and volumes.

The upwards trend in earnings in the third quarter of 1996 continued to strengthen, Veba said and said pre-tax profit in the third quarter was up 16.7 percent on a year-ago, a higher than expected outcome.
Much of the focus in the current year has been on the company's fledgling telecommunications business, still a cost-centre for the group as it attempts to expand its interests in the sector.
Veba said the telecommunications sector made a higher loss during the year, which it said was in line with expectations as it seeks to expand the network.
Early in October, Veba said it was merging its German telecommunications activities with those of fellow utility RWE and British-based Cable & Wireless.
